waypoints.name: The Waterfront River Pub & Terrace
waypoints.notes:
Book a Reservation: https://www.thewaterfrontnapanee.com/#Reservation
Phone: 613-354-2053
thewaterfrontriverpub@gmail.com

Key Features
Menu Highlights: House-made burgers like the Waterfront Double Stack, pulled pork, craft beers on tap, and spiffy cocktails.

Entertainment: Live music performances on Friday and Saturday evenings.

Napanee River Tours: Connected with the docked 45-foot pontoon boat The Norman Paul, allowing visitors to combine river cruises with lunch or dinner packages.

Seasonal Experiences: Outdoor riverside green space in the summer and heated snow globe dining experiences in the colder monthsAfter the pontoon ride from Andy’s we ended up here. 
____________________________________________________
We visited her on the August Long Weekend 2026

The Restaurant is on the river, with many of the tables having a water view. The Napanee river is relatively narrow at this spot and limited docking for boats is available.

The restaurant had a lot of history being an old stone building that had multiple businesses in it over the years.

The food was your typical pub fare, with a few Asian dishes thrown in. 

We were a large party of 14, but we had reservations and were seated quickly. The food, understandably, took a while to arrive, but there was Cornhole and Giant Jenga set up in the courtyard to pass the time waiting for the meals to arrive.

The service was very friendly, we had a new server and I think she did agreat job, especially given the size of our group.

It was a hot day with littel breeze to cool us off, but we were seated mostly in the shade under a pergola.

I would definitely come here again for the ambiance, and the food was good but not great. Rachel had some sort of steak salad bowl that was a great size, though she found a hair in it.

The bathrooms were small and not that clean - they need to check them more often.

I camped here!!  Godd site, would use again.

TRIP TO CROTCH LAKE - SITE 18 - July 18-21

MONDAY - JULY 18, 2022

5:30 - Woke up and was not finished packing despite swearing to. ,myself everything would be packed and ready to go. Loaded up and went towards Guy’s house. The overcast turned to sprinkling by the time I arrived at Guy’s.

Guy did not pack light, I had a my silver Coleman cooler full of food, and Guy had a full bigger white cooler full of ice and beverages. He insisted we had taken two full coolers in the past which we had never done. Guy being Guy, insisted he was right, which he wasn’t. After the trip he went through years of camping pictures to prove his point which he couldn’t :)

Stopped at Tim Hortons in Carleton place for coffee and breakfast sandwiches. Then continued on to Oompah and Crotch lake.

12:13 - Arrived at the lake and loaded the canoe. It might have been a good idea to have a couple of pre-made lunches for the canoe ride.It was raining at this point so we put the tarp over the gear and started off. We did put the two coolers in, but had to pile a lot of equipment on top of the coolers and lash them down. At this point we were a couple of inches out of the water, but luckily the lake was calm. We hugged the left shore and went down the lake drinking our frozen margaritas and searching for campsite 18.

1:30 - Arrived at the campsite 18 after about an hour. It ended up being a nice spot with two fire-pits and lots to fire wood nearby. It was still raining so we quickly strung up the smaller tarp near the dining area, which ended up being a nicely sheltered spot with a plywood table attached to a couple of trees. It was sheltered behind an island, and there was a noisy French family across from us, but they were often away on day trips, so it wasn’t bothersome.

TUESDAY - JULY 19
Set up my custom wood camping table and used it for cooking. The plywood table that was there was very crooked. I need to come up with a better way of attaching the legs, but it worked well.

The weather for the weekend was decent overall, but rain showers would suddenly appear and disappear over the course of the weekend.

Guy wanted to go for a hike around to the next point we could see from our campsite. It ended up being WAY longer and more difficult than we thought because 1) Guy has no sense of direction, and 2) the bay we were trying to hike around was much bigger than we thought and 3) there was no clear path, so there was a lot of bushwhacking going on.

We ended up going fishing from the canoe later and Guy admitted that it would have been easier to canoe to the point rather than hike, but it would have been too easy.

WEDNESDAY - JULY 20
Played lots of games - Crib, Blockus, Uno, 5 Crowns, Darts. Set up 2 hammocks as well, though Guy did not indulge.

THURSDAY - JULY 21
Packed up and left the site. It was windy and the waves, once we left the shelter of the island, were breaking whitecaps about 2 to 3 feet tall. We were heading down the lake at about a 45 degree angle to the wind, and the canoe was still not riding very high in the water, and was top heavy. The waves started breaking over the back of the canoe, and  I was very worried that we were going to take on too much water and flip. We headed towards a nearby island where some ‘good old boys’ were camping. They had brought 2 chainsaws to get firewood to bring back to their island. 

After waiting there a while for the wind to calm down and checking the forecast, we realized it wasn’t going to get better, and maybe even worse. Luckily they were headed back to the boat launch and offered to take some of our gear to lighten our load. Once offloading the gear we were riding higher in the water and were able to cross the lake and rounded the point. Once we were protected from the wind, it was like a totally different lake, calm and easy to paddle and the sun even started to come out.

We made it back safely to the boat launch, but after all of the rain, it was touch and go getting the car out of the edge of the ditch I had parked it in.

TRIP TO CROTCH LAKE - SITE 63 
July 21, 22, 23, 24 - 2023

FRIDAY - JULY 21
Weather report was brutal; calling for torrential rain and washed out roads. As the morning progressed it would rain, then blue sky, rain, then blue sky again. We decided to go for it, and Guy drove to my house and we left from there at 12:00.He had pre-frozen a lot of ice in ziplock bags, but we used his bigger cooler and loaded in all of the ‘refridgerables’.

Driving out of Ottawa and on the way up to the lake it rained on and off, but the wind was relatively light. Missed the turn to the lake, but didn’t go too far past it. It’s now marked on my GPS. By the time we got to the lake at 2:15, there was a bit of sprinkles, but the lake was calm so we decided to go for it. As we were unloading the canoe, It was a bit slippery from the rain and Guy dropped his end on his big toe. Luckily the canoe was ok.

It took him a few minutes of trying not to cry or swear loudly as there were children around, but he eventually pulled himself together and we continued to load the canoe. We were on the lake at 2:45.

We had never been to this site before, and it was much further in than previous sites. Having said that we sipped on our frozen margaritas, and used the trolling motor for much of the way. I kept checking the GPS on my phone (no signal required) and it was a good canoe in, with few waves, and just a bit of rain on and off (mostly off)

Arrived at the site around 4:00 - 1:45 hour paddle in, fully set up with fire going by 5:25. Site 63 was on a rocky point with the lake on one side and a shallow bay on the backside. There was one good spot for the tent which was relatively level with trees in front to string up the tarp. 

There was no camp kitchen set up (usually a piece of plywood between a couple of trees) like at some of the other sites. Luckily I had brought my custom camp kitchen and set that up for the stove. The site was good; Canadian Shield down into the water with weed-free swimming. There were two fire pits, with one up above not he rocky point which we did not use. Great views of the sky from there, and we could see the sunrise, but the sunset was behind the site. There was one other site in the lake/bay we were in, but it was in a shallow bay and did not look very nice.

The sun came out, and there was a beautiful but very shallw/flat rainbow. I've never seen one like it. Guy got the wood together and started the fire while I set up the table, chairs and camp kitchen. We cooked steak on the fire (6:45 - eating at 7:02) and served it with mushrooms and onions and dehydrated mashed potatoes which were very good. Bought a new collapsible measuring cup to add the right amount of boiling water to the potatoes.

SATURDAY - JULY 22
Beautiful day - woke up and got the coffee going, chilled a bit then cooked up the pound of bacon, eggs over easy and 6 potato patties (eating at 8:34). We didn’t cook the sausages for lunch as we weren’t that hungry for some reason. Played games and snacked a bit - I lost every game we played that weekend!

Since the weather was so good, I built a reflector oven to cook the ribs over indirect heat. It worked out well and they were well cooked, but could have been on longer so they would be more ‘fall off the bone’. I was thinking of getting a reflector oven to try baking bread on the site, but it may be overkill? The corn was a bit of a disapointment - a bit too old? We also had coleslaw, but a can of brown beans might have added some extra goodness to the meal. Eating at 8:43 - still light out.

SUNDAY - JULY 23
Up around 7:00 and enjoyed a beautiful morning - weather was perfect, though the mosquitoes and horseflies were annoying. Had OJ and a smoked meat omelette with onions, jalapeños and peppers for breakfast. Guy wanted to go for a hike around the bay - it was the usual slogging though woods - no trails, and Guy had a wipe out and scraped his knee pretty badly. Luckily didn’t bang up his camera too bad. 

At this point Guy is pretty much falling apart; I told him to pull himself together as I was too old to find another camping buddy.

We took a nice paddle around the lake; the maps showed other lakes behind ours, but there was no creek access to them. We played more games which I proceeded to lose. Also spent some time in the hammocks; great for reading and Guy had a nap. We also took a hike along the shoreline which was manageable - no slogging through woods, and we found a deer jaw and pike jaw bones.

Cooked Fajitas for dinner; not a bad idea to have one evening meal that doesn’t rely on the fire (even though the weather was perfect). 

MONDAY - JULY 24
Got up early to another beautiful morning. Made coffee and blueberry pancakes in the new frying pan that I bought a Capella’s with the gift certificate that Guy gave me for my birthday.  Covered the pancakes with whipped cream and more blueberries! We swam every day that weekend and were in the water when the camp people showed up to tell us to leave, this was around 2:00. He said there was another person coming to the site. 

We finished packing, and ate a lunch of ham roll ups in tortillas and coleslaw. We were packed and paddling out by 3:45 and as we paddled out, we saw no one coming in. The camp people may have been fibbing about someone coming just to get us to leave.

Heading out the lake was calm and the wind was light with scattered puffy clouds, I remarked what a nice sky it was and Guy pointed to a dark grey cloud behind us on my right. As I said that the cloud ‘looked grumpy’ there was a loud rumble of thunder. As the storm was behind us we weren’t too concerned, then we heard another rumble from the left side of the canoe. 

At this point we weren’t too far from the boat launch. We arrived and one of the storms continued to get closer as we packed up with thunder crashing overhead. We got into the car and started to drive out just as the rain started; we had timed it perfectly! The ride back to Ottawa was crazy - the rain was intense at times and we could barely see the road at times. Power was off when I arrived home, but came back after an hour or so. 

Fantastic trip; would camp there again!

Trip to Crotch Lake - Site 68 - July 13, 14, 15, 16 2022
 
TUESDAY
There was rain in the forecast for the Tuesday that we went in. When I picked up Guy at 9:20 there was sun in the morning. Loaded the car and were on the Queensway by 10. Stopped in Carleton place for Timmies. Coffee and breakfast sandwiches (Guy’s Treat).   

We got to the lake around 11;30 and loaded up the canoe. When I was parking the car I put it a little too far into the ditch which made it really difficult to get out especially after all the rain that we'd had. We brought a little bit too much stuff as Guy’s camera box and tripod would not easily fit. The table, tent, and pool noodles were strapped sideways across the canoe.  

Leaving the boat ramp we took a turn to the right and went down into a long narrow Mcleans Bay accidentally. We eventually realized that we had turned the wrong way, There were no good unmarked sites in the bay. We put the motor in and went past a 3 sites on the right that were a bit too close together (73,74,75) and were empty at the time they were in view of the boat ramp. There was also a noisy family camping at site 76, a short distance from the boat ramp.  

As we went down the lake it started to cloud over rather rapidly. The water was calm until we rounded the point at site 70, heading towards site 69 and 68. It was if it was another lake altogether. The wind and waves were picking up, and we were going into a headwind. Glad to have the motor. People were camping at site 69; 4 older German sounding people. 
 
We arrived at site 68 around 1:00; the docking was a bit difficult and rocky but we unloaded the canoe sideways against a sheet of rock. It was a short haul up to the site and we were surprised to see a picnic table. 

We quickly set up the tent and strung up one of my new big tarps over the picnic table. Guy also gathered a bit of wood which we put under a small tarp to keep it dry. 

Just as we finished doing this the sky opened up and we had a massive thunder storm. We ate smoked meat sandwiches under the tarp and played crib. Guy skunked me the first game, but in the cribbage series over the next few days, we ended up tied.  

The rain stopped and we finished setting up camp. I set up the new camp kitchen that I built and it worked great. I need to improve the way the legs attach to the table top, but it was a joy to use for meal prep. We disconnected the Backgammon board and played a best of 7 series. I won the first game, but then Guy won the next three. Just as he was starting to feel cocky I won the next 3 games (best 4 of 7) and won the series. Guy kept his tears hidden but I think he died a little bit inside in that moment.  

The weather cleared up and we did cedar planked rainbow trout fillets on a bed of lemon slices, green beans and basmati rice. The rice was pre-cooked in plastic pouches and was heated up in the kettle full of water. 2 pouches was sufficient. 

We sat by the fire that night and turned in about 11:00. Slept OK on new air mattresses and was warm in my new sleeping bag.

WEDNESDAY 
Woke at 6:30, made coffee in the percolator. Made 6 eggs over easy, a package of bacon and 6 potato patties. Hung around the site, was a clear day with wind, so didn’t canoe around that day. 

Played Kulami; Guy won a couple and I tied a couple. Played a new card game; 5 Crowns, and I won that one. Lots of wild cards, was a fun game.  

Lunch on the fire; 4 Italian hot sausages with coleslaw and potato salad. We could have done 1 sausage each instead of 2.   

Dinner was Ribs, precooked at home in beer. The fire was being difficult so warming the ribs up was not as easy as it should have been, but they tasted fine. We ate late in the dark (9:00?) as we had lunch at 2:30 and were still full.  Slept a bit better the second night; and it rained during the night. 

THURSDAY
Woke up early again. Made coffee and a 6 egg omelette with cheese, red and yellow bell peppers and a few spicy peppers. 

The lake was calm with little wind so we paddled over to Kings Lake Dam. We passed a couple of island sites (12,13) and got out and explored 14. It’s an interesting site but getting the gear up to it would be a bit difficult as it was steep and a bit slippery. Interesting site though, with a good fire pit area and sheltered picnic table. 

We fished a bit on the way there and back. A few nibbles but no fish. We decided to skip lunch (Fajitas) so we would be hungry for the steak dinner.  We had a nice dinner before dark; the steaks were very good and decently tender. Served with coleslaw and potato salad. 

FRIDAY 
Next day was sunny and the gear had time to dry out. We skipped the blueberry pancakes for breakfast and had the fajitas as a brunch. We packed up the site and had a nice paddle out, in calm, sunny weather. 

Left the lake around 3:00 and were back in Ottawa around 5:30.

I’ve camped here - great site!!

**August 15 - 2020**
Beautiful trip with Guy and Emma. Crotch Lake site 69. Short drive down from Oompah to the lake. Missed the turn-off and had to backtrack to find South Bush Road. 

With three poeple bought a $19 inflatable kids boat from Walmart and towed Emma behind the Canoe. Emma was wearing her pink cowboy hat and I handed her a frozen Margarita as she climbed in to the boat. The people loading their canoes next to us with minimal gear for a long portage laden trip looked at all the gear we were bringing and were a bit shocked. One girl said "I want to go camping with them - It looks like they will be having more fun!" 

Site 69 was amazing; Canadian Shield slabs on the point. Big site. Nice view of the sunrise. Great swimming, no weeds not slippery on the rocks and deep drop off. It was a bit windy being exposed on the point. Nice spots in the trees for tents, could do 3 tents there.

Loaded up the canoe and an inflatable raft to tow Emma. Emma enjoyed the ride, wore her pink. Cowboy hat and read her book. Lot of stuff - shockingly too many cans of drinks.

Friday and Saturday were beautiful, stars were amazing on Friday night in the dark sky preserve, Saturday night had a few clouds.

Sunday started off clear but clouded over quickly. Big thunder storm started at 11:00, with whitecaps on the lake. Passed by at 1:00. We started to pack up when the rain started, but it started to pour so we stopped. I quickly set up a tarp over the main area, and had to defend from the big puddles that started to form on the tarp. 

Surprisingly the tarp was not waterproof, and we did see some dripping underneath the pools on top of it, so it was important to keep moving the water off the tarp. Emma came down to help, while Guy took a nice nap in his tent. Good thing as there wasn’t much extra room under the tarp. Tents did not leak. Storm passed after an hour or so, then we packed up and left the site at 3:10, arrived at boat launch at 3:40. Paddled out in flat water and calm winds 30 minute canoe to the site. 

Windscreen on the stove needs to be re-taped. Cedar planked salmon on the fire worked well; covered the entire thing top and bottom with aluminum foil so it cooked evenly and the plank did not catch on fire. Hollandaise and green beans went well. Need new aluminum foil and new dartboard, the rain destroyed it.

Camping Olympics:
Guy won first game of crib, but it was close. I won the next two, Emma joined in and we played three handed. Skunked Emma one game, and won the second game as well. So I won the Crib event.

Uno
After we figured out the rules,  Emma was doing the best at Uno; Guy complained that we were ganging up on him, but only because he was a big baby.

Farkle
Guy went over 10000 first and we all had one more chance to catch up and beat him. Both Emma and I were far behind, more than 4000 points behind.. Emma started well, but soon Farkeled. Then I one on a great roll and made more than the 4500 that I needed to beat Guy. Guy then tried one more roll to beat me, but ended up 50 points short before he Farkled.

Golf
Card game - It started to rain before we finished the second round. Guy hit 50 first and was knocked out. I won.
